description: Official LuciferCore framework: A high-performance, fully asynchronous .NET ecosystem designed for Modulith architectures. Fuses Data-Oriented Design (DOD) with high-speed OOP pooling to achieve zero-allocation pipelines and maximum CPU cache locality. Powered by a lock-free Buffer-Model architecture and a lightweight static DI container designed to fully saturate multi-core hardware. Automating infrastructure so you can focus 100% on core logic.
releaseNotes:
[Major Architectural Refactoring - LuciferCore v3.0]

      - Total Worker-based Pipeline Removal: Completely transitioned to an I/O-driven, non-queued execution model. "Task-based Worker" pools have been officially eliminated from the request pipeline to prevent RAM bloat and scheduling overhead, resulting in a dramatic performance boost.
      - High-Performance Callback Pipeline: Implemented a "Callback-only" execution path for standard requests. API and Static file processing latency are now nearly identical, reaching 140,000+ req/s in resource-constrained environments.
      - Optimized Memory Management: Effectively eliminated "RAM bloat" during high-traffic spikes by removing queued job storage. The system now processes requests in a streaming fashion, keeping memory usage stable and flat under load.
      - Decoupled SimulationManager: Reduced to a lightweight, independent event scheduler for critical sequential operations. It no longer acts as a global bottleneck and operates asynchronously from the core Handler logic, ensuring high maintainability.
      - Background WorkerManager: Task Workers are now strictly relegated to independent background maintenance/housekeeping tasks only. They are no longer involved in the request handling lifecycle.
      - Session-Local Rate Limiting: Replaced global/method-level rate limiting with session-based local throttling to remove lock contention on global objects, allowing the system to scale linearly with concurrent connections.

      [Future Roadmap]
      - Thread-Local Caching: Preparing to implement high-speed thread-local caching for frequently accessed routes and static files, trading a minimal amount of memory for even greater throughput in future releases.
title: LuciferCore by thuangf45: High-Performance Zero-Allocation Framework
